cases.requirement: M4-044 preserves M4-023 as the portable approval-routing authority and M4-042 as the Adapter DSH native ToolRuntime approval authority; Harness remains compatibility evidence only.

Multiple approval-named ports, entry points, observers, fixtures, or test fakes are not by themselves duplicate subsystems; duplicate ownership requires competing automatic orchestration/state for the same logical approval attempt.
M4-023 policy allow and deny paths do not invoke ApprovalInvocationPort.
M4-023 invokes exactly one supplied ApprovalInvocationPort for an accepted ask path after accepted Lease-result validation.
M4-023 has no automatic retry, remembered approval, permanent grant, approval queue, approval cache, or fallback provider.
Capability Broker production code does not import concrete Adapter DSH or DeepSeek Harness approval orchestration types.
Adapter registerToolPolicy projects safe-runtime ASK into Harness pre-execute ask and does not invoke Adapter requestApproval for the same ASK.
One final/reached ToolRuntime ASK is owned by the pinned native ToolRuntime serviceAsk -> ctx.approval.request path.
One real final/reached ToolRuntime ASK produces exactly one native ApprovalService request.
The same ToolRuntime ASK produces exactly one native approval/asked record and one approval/decided record with the same service-owned approval identity.
The exactly-one ToolRuntime request and asked/decided pair are proven in one execution so uniqueness is not assembled from unrelated tests or commits.
Adapter requestApproval is an explicit caller-selected entry point into the same ctx.approval Harness ApprovalService rather than a separately configured approval provider.
One explicit Adapter requestApproval invocation reaches ctx.approval.request exactly once and does not originate ToolRuntime execution or a tools/pre-execute ASK.
If ctx.approval is absent, explicit Adapter requestApproval returns UNAVAILABLE without inventing a second provider or approval state.
Native Harness ApprovalService owns ApprovalRequestId and approval/asked -> approval/decided lifecycle; Adapter observation does not create a second native approval identity store.
Portable requestRef/actionRef remain opaque and are not inferred to equal Harness callId or ApprovalRequestId in order to join independent approval subsystems.
REJECTED, CANCELLED and UNAVAILABLE are not automatically retried through a second approval provider.
ALLOWED_ONCE is not remembered, cached, promoted to ALLOWED_ALWAYS or converted into a durable grant by M4-044.
The M3 fake approval service remains test-only infrastructure and is not imported or wired as a production approval owner.
Adapter DSH production code does not import testkit approval fakes as a fallback or alternate approval service.
No production approval cache, remembered-grant store, automatic fallback provider, second queue, or second asked/decided lifecycle is introduced by M4-044.

A concrete production duplicate discovered by the audit must be fixed minimally only after the protocol-first exact head is dual-green; absence of a duplicate requires no speculative production rewrite.
All Harness runtime claims are proven against exact 0.1.0-rc.5 commit 47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a rather than newer/default-branch behavior.
M4-044 neither claims arbitrary callers cannot deliberately double-invoke approval APIs nor implements M4-045 audit redaction, M4-050+ negative boundaries, M5 ledger behavior, or PR #3 merge.
